stumbles.quote: thick film sinks toward the tilt and thin film rises
stumbles.why: "Toward the tilt" is unclear: tilt is an angle, not a place. It's not obvious which direction the film moves, or what is being tilted (the device or the film).

stumbles.quote: Colour matches a reference at mean ΔE76 0.07.
stumbles.why: The text never says what the reference is (a photo, a physical film, a model?). ΔE76 is also jargon to many developers. I can't tell whether 0.07 is good, and it's suspiciously small.

stumbles.quote: goes black from the top and pops
stumbles.why: Black at the top is not explained. A reader who doesn't know thin-film interference won't know that very thin film looks black just before it bursts.

stumbles.quote: Checked headless on a software GPU, not a phone.
stumbles.why: It's unclear what was checked: the colour match, the behaviour, or just that it runs. It's also unclear whether this means the demo is untested or broken on phones and real GPUs.

point: A WebGPU soap-film simulation where thickness acts as density, so the film drains, thins, goes black and pops. Its colour is claimed to match a reference closely, but it was tested only on a software GPU, not on a phone.
